title: Heap Allocation [Practice]
description:
## Practice: Dynamic Array
Let's use `brk` to build a simple dynamic array on the heap.

Your goal: allocate space for 4 qwords (32 bytes), store the values 10, 20, 30, 40, then sum them and print the result.

### Reminder:
```asm
; allocate
mov rax, 12
mov rdi, 0
syscall          ; rax = current break
mov r12, rax     ; save base
lea rdi, [rax + 32]
mov rax, 12
syscall          ; allocate 32 bytes

; store values
mov qword [r12],      10
mov qword [r12 + 8],  20
mov qword [r12 + 16], 30
mov qword [r12 + 24], 40

; access by index: address = base + (index * 8)
```

---
## Assignment:
Allocate 32 bytes on the heap. Store 10, 20, 30, 40 as qwords. Sum all four values. Print `PASS` if the sum equals 100.
setupCode:
section .data
    s_pass db "PASS", 10
    s_pass_len equ $ - s_pass
    s_fail db "FAIL", 10
    s_fail_len equ $ - s_fail

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
_start:
    ; allocate 32 bytes on heap

    ; store 10, 20, 30, 40

    ; sum all four values

    ; check if sum == 100, print PASS or FAIL

    ; exit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Use r12 for the base address. Store with mov qword [r12 + offset], value. Sum into rax by adding each [r12 + offset].
